messages:
ryan: Heads-up — FinSys (enterprise) asked for a formal capacity plan ahead of next-week POC. They want guidance on reserved GPUs, autoscale behavior, and a pricing rough-order-of-magnitude. POC traffic will simulate production surge. Can we draft a short runbook by EOD?

ana: +1. Need the traffic profile and failure SLOs. Do we have the sequence length distribution and peak concurrency?

ryan: Quick profile from AE: ~50k req/day, baseline 10 req/s, peak 220 req/s sustained for ~30m windows. Token distribution: 60% short (<128), 30% medium (128–512), 10% long (~1024). 95th latency target <= 300ms for generation up to 512 tokens.

sales_ops_bot: checklist: 1) baseline pool sizing, 2) prewarm strategy, 3) autoscale policy + burst credits, 4) pricing band for commit vs usage. Attach any config snippets as code.

infra_oncall: Ok — initial intuition: reserved pool for commit + autoscale for bursts. Recommend dedicated GPU pool with GPU type tuned to model. Two quick options:
- conservative (latency SLO focus): 4 x A100-80GB reserved, prewarm 2, autoscale max 16 with burst credits.
- cost-optimized (higher latency tail acceptable): 2 x A100 reserved, prewarm 1, autoscale max 8.

infra_oncall: sample autoscale snippet we can hand them: 

```
# capacity proposal (YAML)
dedicated_pool:
  model: redwood-13B-q4
  gpu_type: a100-80
  reserved_gpus: 4
  prewarm_instances: 2
  autoscale:
    min_instances: 2
    max_instances: 16
    scale_policy: latency_p90
    burst_credits: 3000
```

infra_oncall: rough perf multipliers: 1 A100 (80GB) ~ handles ~40–60 concurrent 512-token gen requests depending on batching and kv-cache reuse. So 4 gpus -> ~160–240 concurrent. With queue-aware autoscale we cover 220 req/s peak if average RT ~200–300ms.

marco: For pricing, customer asked for a commit discount band. How do we present commit vs on-demand? I can draft a table but need unit economics.

ana: Simple calc so sales has a ballpark: assume average generation 200 tokens per request (weighted by distribution). If model cost roughly $0.0001 per token on hosted baseline, then 50k req/day * 200 tokens = 10M tokens/day -> $1,000/day hosted equivalent. But with dedicated + quantization we can push infra cost much lower — show committed reserved GPU monthly rate + variable usage for bursts.

marco: Can we convert the GPU pool to a monthly commit estimate? Example: 4 x A100 reserved -> monthly infra list $X (cloud) + Redwood infra surcharge Y. I'll prepare three tiers: dev-preview (2 gpus), prod-min (4 gpus), prod-plus (8 gpus).

lea: Also flag security questionnaire: FinSys will ask about data isolation/ingress. For Dedicated we need to confirm VPC peering + KMS for keys. I'll start a short answer bundle they can paste in their SecQ.

ryan: Important enterprise blocker: FinSys legal wants SLA language for guaranteed throughput for bursts during trading hours. Can we propose a prewarm + standby credits approach instead of hard throughput SLA? That is easier to guarantee operationally.

infra_oncall: Yes — propose: dedicated prewarm of N instances during trading hours + a standby burst pool with guaranteed credit tokens. Example policy: prewarm 2 across AZs 09:00–17:00 + reserved burst credits sufficient for 15 minutes at 500 qps. If they need hard throughput SLA, we require larger commit or colocated warm standby.

ana: Quick math for burst credits: 500 qps * 60s * average 200 tokens = 6M tokens for 1 minute. For 15 minutes = 90M tokens. If token-processing cost on committed infra ~ $0.00002/token -> 90M * 0.00002 = $1,800 for the 15m burst support. Use that to frame 'burst credit' pricing.

marco: Good. I'll include 3 pricing callouts: 1) reserved pool monthly flat, 2) burst credits bucket (prepaid), 3) overage per-token. That usually closes legal asks.

infra_oncall: One more operational note: enable prefix caching for the POC prompt set — we can reduce effective tokens per request for repeat patterns. Recommend adding KV cache layer in the POC config.

ryan: Action items:
- marco: put together commit tiers + ballpark numbers by 5pm PT.
- ana: finish traffic sim plan for POC and confirm seq-length histogram.
- lea: SecQ answers + confirmation on KMS/VPC wording.
- infra_oncall: finalize YAML + autoscale policy and validate with SRE runbook.

lea: Got it. I can also add a one-paragraph note explaining why we recommend burst credits vs hard throughput SLA (operationally feasible + predictable cost).

marco: I'll post the draft pricing doc in this thread when done. If anyone has objections to the 4xA100 baseline, shout now.

ryan: No objections from me. If FinSys pushes for lower commit, we can propose the 2x baseline + higher burst credits as compromise.

sales_ops_bot: remind: add the POC runbook to the deal folder and tag #enterprise-commits. :white_check_mark:

ryan: Thanks all — will sync with AE and FinSys tomorrow.
